key_insight: A trust-limited Gaussian-process surrogate can accelerate NEB path finding for small-polaron hopping in rutile TiO2 while still preserving first-principles accuracy near difficult charge-transfer regions.
engineering_relevance: This workflow enables reproducible migration-barrier calculations for strongly coupled electron-lattice systems, reducing expensive DFT sampling while maintaining reliable transition-path verification.
method: Joint energy-force Gaussian process with Matérn covariance guides NEB image updates
Active-atom RMS and max-displacement trust limits trigger DFT sampling before the surrogate strays too far
Independent DFT verification is used to confirm final barriers and force convergence
evidence_signal: Three verified 96-atom runs produced consistent barriers of 0.1645, 0.1637, and 0.1640 eV, and a larger 324-atom run gave 0.1302 eV, showing both reproducibility and supercell sensitivity.
watch_item: Surrogate stability can still be challenged by localization switching and repeated central-image sampling, so local GP calibration and full-band DFT checks remain important.
paper_title: Trust-Limited Machine-Learning-Accelerated Nudged Elastic Band Calculations for Small-Polaron Hopping in Rutile TiO2
